scale: Every technology score is an integer from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent) for that criterion. Scores are curated by hand from the vendor documents listed on each technology; they are judgements anchored to the definitions below, not measurements.

ease.meaning: How gentle the learning curve and first setup are
ease.1: Weeks of study before a first working feature
ease.3: A few days with the official tutorial
ease.5: A working app in an afternoon from a quickstart

ops.meaning: How little operational work the team does (patching, scaling, backups)
ops.1: The team runs servers, upgrades and backups itself
ops.3: Managed service, but the team tunes capacity and configuration
ops.5: Fully managed; nothing to patch or scale by hand

maturity.meaning: Years in production use, stability of the API, size of the ecosystem
maturity.1: Under 2 years old or breaking changes every release
maturity.3: 3 to 7 years, stable core, smaller ecosystem
maturity.5: 10+ years, long-term support releases, very large ecosystem

performance.meaning: Typical speed and resource use under load for this layer
performance.1: Noticeably slower or heavier than peers in public benchmarks
performance.5: Among the fastest in its category in public benchmarks

scalability.meaning: How far it grows before a redesign is needed
scalability.1: Single machine or tens of requests per second
scalability.3: Thousands of requests per second with standard tuning
scalability.5: Documented use at hundreds of thousands of requests per second or more

realtime.meaning: Support for long-lived connections and live updates
realtime.3: Possible with an add-on service or beta feature
realtime.5: Built in and documented for production use

seo.3: Server rendering available but not the default or needs extra setup
seo.5: Server or static rendering by default

velocity.meaning: How quickly a small team ships features
velocity.1: Much boilerplate; every feature is custom work
velocity.3: Good libraries for common needs, some glue code
velocity.5: Batteries included: auth, data access and admin come ready

hiring.meaning: Size of the pool of developers who already know it
hiring.1: Fewer than 1 in 50 developers in public surveys

structure.meaning: Support for keeping a large codebase organised
structure.1: No conventions; structure is up to each developer
structure.5: Opinionated structure enforced by the framework

interactivity.meaning: Fit for rich, stateful user interfaces
interactivity.3: Sprinkled interactivity with some client state
interactivity.5: Component model built for complex client state

offline.meaning: Support for working without a network connection
offline.1: Needs a connection at all times
offline.3: Can cache data; sync is hand-written
